tagline: Kyndryl is the world's largest IT infrastructure services provider offering mission-critical enterprise technology services.
hero_kpi_rationale: Total revenue is the fundamental KPI reflecting Kyndryl's overall performance as a global leader in IT infrastructure services, with a diversified customer base and critical long-term contracts.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales of goods and services generated by the company.
kpis.description: Total revenue represents the total amount of sales from the company's goods and services.
kpis.signal: Decline in revenue for fiscal year 2025, due to efforts to reduce low-margin contracts.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Total profit after deduction of all expenses.
kpis.description: Net income is the final profit after all expenses, taxes, and interest.
kpis.signal: Significant improvement in net income compared to the prior year, impacted by the gain from the sale of the SIS platform in Canada.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, adjusted for non-operational items.
kpis.description: Measures operating performance before non-cash and non-recurring items.
kpis.signal: Growth in Adjusted EBITDA, indicating improved operational performance and efficiency.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Gross margin is a key indicator of profitability before operating expenses.
kpis.signal: Not available in the provided 10-K. Kyndryl does not break down gross margin in its public financial statements.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Operating margin measures the profitability of a company's core operations.
kpis.signal: Not available in the provided 10-K. Kyndryl uses Adjusted EBITDA as its key measure of operational performance.

kpis.name: R&D Investments (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Spending on research and development expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Indicates the company's commitment to innovation and development of new technologies.
kpis.signal: Not available in the provided 10-K. As an IT services provider, Kyndryl does not separately disclose R&D expenses.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on tangible and intangible assets to maintain and improve infrastructure.
kpis.description: Represents funds used by the company to acquire or upgrade its long-term physical assets.
kpis.signal: Not quantified in the provided 10-K. The document mentions 10.9 million square feet of owned or leased space (data centers and offices) but no specific capex figures.

kpis.name: Recurring Managed Services Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from ongoing, long-term managed services.
kpis.description: Recurring revenue from long-term managed services, more predictable and stable than project-based services.
kpis.signal: Not specifically quantified in the 10-K. Kyndryl offers managed services across its business areas (cloud, data, AI, etc.) but does not break out recurring revenue separately.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees working for the company.
kpis.description: The number of employees reflects the scale of operations and investments in human capital. Kyndryl operates with a hybrid model combining global and local talent.
kpis.signal: The 10-K mentions 'tens of thousands of skilled practitioners' but provides no exact headcount figure.

kpis.name: Cloud and AI Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from cloud, data, and artificial intelligence services.
kpis.description: Revenue from cloud, data, and artificial intelligence services, a key strategic area for Kyndryl in its transformation toward new technology paradigms.
kpis.signal: Kyndryl offers services in 'cloud services' and 'data and AI services' explicitly mentioned in the 10-K, but revenue is not broken down by specific technology segment.

kpis.name: Percentage of Deals Including AI Features
kpis.explanation: Percentage of new customer contracts that include artificial intelligence components.
kpis.description: Indicator of customer adoption of AI solutions in their IT and digital transformations.
kpis.signal: No quantified data available in the 10-K for fiscal year 2025. Kyndryl positions AI as a key area but provides no public penetration metrics.

kpis.name: Volume of AI API Calls
kpis.explanation: Volume of calls to artificial intelligence application programming interfaces used by Kyndryl's customers.
kpis.description: Measures customer usage of Kyndryl's AI services, an indirect indicator of increasing adoption of AI solutions in production.
kpis.signal: No data available in the 10-K for fiscal year 2025. Kyndryl does not disclose AI API usage metrics.

risks.title: Continuing Revenue Decline
risks.score_rationale: The document reports a 6% revenue decline in 2025, following -6% in 2024 and -7% in 2023. Repeated language about revenue declines across all key segments indicates a structural trend. The Capital category is heavily weighted here due to impact on long-term viability.

risks.title: Margin Pressure
risks.score_rationale: The text repeatedly cites actions to reduce low-margin components of customer relationships. This indicates persistent pressure on profitability. The language is recurring and strategic, underscoring the risk's significance.

risks.title: Exposure to Currency Fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the impact of exchange rates on revenue, particularly in Japan. The risk is cited as a factor in revenue decline, with precise and recurring language, and the Macro category is highly significant.

risks.title: Dependence on Operational Transformation
risks.score_rationale: Margin and EBITDA improvements are attributed to operational efficiency gains. Future success therefore depends on the continuation of these initiatives, a central theme in management's messaging. The language is strategic and repeated.

risks.title: Risks Related to IBM Separation
risks.score_rationale: The separation from IBM is mentioned as a foundational event, with past transaction costs. While less prominent in 2025, the risk of residual dependency or competition with IBM is implicit. The language is factual but dated.

risks.title: Geopolitical Market Volatility
risks.score_rationale: The document cites geopolitical tensions, tariffs, and reduced public spending as sources of economic uncertainty. The language is alarmist ('volatility', 'concerns') and recent, reinforcing the severity.

ai_positioning.summary: Company KD does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
